body:
Installation logging fails on steps 2-5 due to incorrect global variable usage with session references. Demo data flag is saved but never executed. Uninstallation always shows confirmation screen without progressing to execution.

## Changes

### Fixed session reference logging
Functions used `global $installData` which fails with `$installData = &$_SESSION[...]`. Changed to direct session access:

```php
// Before (broken)
function installLog(string $message, string $type = 'info'): void
{
    global $installData;  // Doesn't work with references
    $installData['log'][] = ['message' => $message, 'type' => $type];
}

// After (working)
function installLog(string $message, string $type = 'info'): void
{
    $_SESSION['PROSPEKTWEB_CALC_INSTALL']['log'][] = ['message' => $message, 'type' => $type];
}
```

Applied to `installLog()`, `createIblockTypeWithLog()`, `createIblockWithLog()`, `createSkuRelationWithLog()`.

### Added demo data creation
Integrated existing `DemoDataCreator` class in step 4 after settings save. Includes validation for class existence and populated iblock IDs.

### Fixed uninstallation routing
Added step parameter handling to `DoUninstall()` matching `DoInstall()` pattern:

```php
$step = (int)($_REQUEST['step'] ?? 1);
switch ($step) {
    case 1: // Show confirmation (unstep1.php)
    case 2: // Execute uninstall (unstep2.php)
    default: // Fallback to confirmation
}
```

# Add dynamic OG image generator for marketing pages

## Summary
This PR adds a dynamic Open Graph image generator using Next.js's `ImageResponse` API. Instead of using static `/og-image.png` files, pages now generate branded OG images with:
- The Taylored Instruction logo
- Dynamic title and description text
- Location badges for Vancouver, WA and San Luis Obispo, CA
- A branded footer with certification affiliations
- Accent color variations based on page type (red for AHA courses, blue for lifeguarding)

**Files changed:**
- `app/api/og/route.tsx` - New API route that generates 1200x630 OG images
- `lib/utils.ts` - Added `generateOgImageUrl` helper function
- Updated all 17 marketing pages to use dynamic OG images

## Updates since last revision
- Removed `runtime = "edge"` config that was incompatible with `nextConfig.cacheComponents`
- Fixed logo path from `/public/Logo-Black.png` to `/Logo-Black.png`
- Tested locally and verified OG images render correctly with logo
- **Added dynamic OG images to all remaining public pages** (10 additional pages: basic-life-support, aeds, corporate-training, alignment, terms, privacy-policy, fa-cpr-aed-instructor, lifeguarding-instructor-trainer, lifeguarding-instructor, aha-instructor-training)
- Added missing `openGraph` and `twitter` metadata to terms and privacy-policy pages

![Local test of OG image generator](https://app.devin.ai/api/presigned_proxy?token=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9..ifcEKb-2TxErVHsL4q3-1Z7KYLcDZ6f8CrU8bjEyzLI)

## Review & Testing Checklist for Human
- [ ] **Verify logo loads in production** - The logo URL is constructed dynamically; confirm it renders correctly on Vercel (not just localhost). This was a bug that was fixed.
- [ ] **Visual inspection of generated images** - Visit `/api/og?title=Test%20Title&description=Test%20Description&type=bls` on the preview deployment and verify the layout looks good, text doesn't overflow, and colors are correct
- [ ] **Test actual social sharing** - Use a social media debugger (e.g., https://cards-dev.twitter.com/validator or Facebook Sharing Debugger) to test OG image rendering for a few pages
- [ ] **Verify terms/privacy-policy metadata** - These pages now have openGraph/twitter metadata that they didn't have before

**Recommended test plan:**
1. Deploy to preview environment
2. Visit `https://[preview-url]/api/og?title=BLS%20Certification&description=Healthcare%20Training&type=bls`
3. Use Facebook Sharing Debugger or Twitter Card Validator to test actual OG image rendering for a few pages (homepage, BLS, terms)

### Notes
- The OG images use system fonts rather than the site's Readex Pro font (limitation of ImageResponse API)

author: amkcode
body:
**Description of changes:**
This PR implements program partitioning for the Mirage superoptimizer. Mirage can dramatically improve kernel performance through superoptimization, but exploring its enormous configuration search space is computationally expensive. To keep optimization time manageable—especially for large models—we need to carefully limit the operators included in each superoptimization run. This makes the question of how to partition a full computational graph into Mirage-optimizable subgraphs a crucial one. Suboptimal partitioning can leave significant performance improvements untapped.

In this PR, we introduce a cost-model-driven partitioning method that applies dynamic programming to recursively split arbitrary computational graphs into subgraphs that Mirage can efficiently superoptimize . We evaluated our framework on a transformer-based model and observed speedups of up to 1.17× over vanilla PyTorch.

Our key contributions include:
	•	A dataset of subgraphs, their superoptimized kernels, and execution times, extracted from open-source models (Qwen, Gemma, Llama, CLIP).
	•	A ML cost model that predicts superoptimized execution time for unseen subgraphs.
	•	A full framework that ingests arbitrary PyTorch programs, performs cost-model-guided partitioning and superoptimization, and outputs an executable program enhanced with Mirage-optimized kernels.

body:
### Added

- **RecordId + RecordKey Architecture (Issue #60)**: Complete rewrite of internal storage for stable record identification
  - `RecordId`: u32 index wrapper for O(1) Vec-based hot-path access
  - `RecordKey`: Hybrid `&'static str` / `Arc<str>` with `Borrow<str>` for zero-alloc static keys and flexible dynamic keys
  - O(1) key resolution via `HashMap<RecordKey, RecordId>`
  - Type introspection via `HashMap<TypeId, Vec<RecordId>>`
- **Key-Based Producer/Consumer API**:
  - `produce_by_key::<T>(key, value)`: Produce to specific record by key
  - `subscribe_by_key::<T>(key)`: Subscribe to specific record by key  
  - `producer_by_key::<T>(key)`: Get key-bound producer
  - `consumer_by_key::<T>(key)`: Get key-bound consumer
- **New Types**: `ProducerByKey<T, R>` and `ConsumerByKey<T, R>` for key-bound access with `.key()` accessor
- **Introspection Methods**:
  - `records_of_type::<T>()`: Returns `&[RecordId]` for all records of type T
  - `resolve_key(key)`: O(1) lookup returning `Option<RecordId>`
- **New Error Variants**:
  - `RecordKeyNotFound`: Key doesn't exist in registry
  - `InvalidRecordId`: RecordId out of bounds  
  - `TypeMismatch`: Type assertion failed during downcast
  - `AmbiguousType`: Multiple records of same type (use key-based API)
  - `DuplicateRecordKey`: Key already registered
- **RecordMetadata Extensions**: Now includes `record_id: u32` and `record_key: String` fields

### Changed

- **Breaking: `configure<T>()` Signature**: Now requires key parameter: `configure::<T>("key", |reg| ...)`
- **Breaking: Internal Storage**: Changed from `BTreeMap<TypeId, Box<dyn AnyRecord>>` to:
  - `Vec<Box<dyn AnyRecord>>` for O(1) hot-path access by RecordId
  - `HashMap<RecordKey, RecordId>` for O(1) name lookups
  - `HashMap<TypeId, Vec<RecordId>>` for type introspection
- **Breaking: Type-Based Lookup**: `produce()`, `subscribe()`, `producer()`, `consumer()` now return `AmbiguousType` error when multiple records of the same type exist
- **SecurityPolicy**: `ReadWrite` variant now uses `HashSet<String>` for writable record keys
- **Dependencies**: Added `hashbrown` for no_std-compatible HashMap with `default-hasher` feature

## Description

Fixes #11071

Requested by: danny@buildwithfern.com (@dannysheridan)
Link to Devin run: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/628aefbac8d2421a963098b72abc5d98

When a schema with top-level `nullable: true` is referenced via `allOf` inheritance, `fern generate` crashes with an error like:
```
Failed to load type declaration for type type_:nullable<SomeType>
```

The root cause is that the OpenAPI importer was including `nullable<>` wrappers in type references when building the extends list, but the actual type declarations in the IR exist without the wrapper (e.g., `type_:SomeType` not `type_:nullable<SomeType>`).

## Changes Made

- Added `stripNullableWrapperForExtends` helper function that removes `nullable<>` and `optional<nullable<>>` wrappers from type strings
- Applied the helper when building extends lists in:
  - `buildTypeDeclaration.ts` (for object type allOf schemas and inlined schemas)
  - `buildEndpoint.ts` (for request body extends)
- Added changelog entry for version 3.4.2

## Testing

- [x] Manual testing completed - verified the reproduction case from the issue now generates IR correctly with `type_:NullableObject` instead of `type_:nullable<NullableObject>` in the extends list
- [ ] Unit tests added/updated - no automated test fixture added

## Human Review Checklist

- [ ] Verify the regex patterns in `stripNullableWrapperForExtends` handle edge cases correctly (nested types, unusual type names)
- [ ] Confirm that unconditionally stripping nullable wrappers from extends is semantically correct (you extend the underlying type, not a nullable wrapper)
- [ ] Consider whether a seed test fixture should be added to prevent regression

This major update extends the chatbot's capabilities beyond FAQ support by enabling 
semantic search over the product catalogue and preparing the foundation for intelligent

  - Introduced `/api/v1/ingest/products` endpoint for indexing products.
  - Ensures correct vector dimension (384) and uses numeric IDs for Qdrant compatibility.

• Product semantic retriever
  - Added `ProductRetrieverService` to support semantic queries over products.
  - Returns product metadata along with similarity scores.

• Chatbot product-search intent
  - Updated ChatService to route PRODUCT_SEARCH requests to the semantic retriever.
  - Added formatted multi-product response (“Voici quelques produits ShopyVerse…”).
  - Updated session history to include product recommendations.
  - NLU now fully supports FAQ / PRODUCT_SEARCH / OTHER flows.

• Utility improvements
  - Clear logging for intent detection and product indexing.
  - Added optional test route for semantic product search (for local validation).

This prepares the way for:
  - Full product recommendation features,
  - Multi-modal product ranking,
  - Real-time catalogue synchronisation from the core API,
  - Enhanced conversational commerce capabilities inside ShopyVerse.

author: o-az
body:
1. the loader was awaiting `holdersSummary` before rendering. This blocked the entire page on the slow holders query. Changed to `prefetchQuery` so the page renders immediately while sidebar stats load in background.
2. The holders tab still awaited `ensureQueryData` for holders data before rendering. Changed to `prefetchQuery` + `useQuery` in the component so the tab renders immediately with a loading state.

There are two strategies:

1. awaited `queryClient.ensureQueryData` in loader + `useLoaderData` in component
2. non-awaited `queryClient.prefetchQuery` in loader + `useQuery` in component

The first one is render-blocking, the 2nd lets the page load instantly. We should favor the 2nd one, especially for paginated routes.

Another option is firing `ensureQueryData` without awaiting it and then using `<Await>` component.
